name: Steppe
notes: Cold, semi-arid temperate grassland of feather grasses, fescues and wormwoods with rare shrubs, treeless except ravines; Eurasian steppe (Ukraine to Mongolia) with Patagonian and Great Basin analogues.

canopy.name: Siberian elm
canopy.origin: Central Asia, Mongolia and N China
canopy.source: Ulmus pumila, Central Asia/Mongolia/N China steppe ravines and river banks, 10-25 m — Flora of China

traits.native_range: Ulmus pumila, Central Asia/Mongolia/N China steppe ravines and river banks, 10-25 m — Flora of China
traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

canopy.silhouette: open rounded crown of small leaves, brittle limbs

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two small oblong cotyledons, then alternate, small (2-5 cm), singly toothed, almost symmetrical elm leaves on a thin zigzag stem. Saplings are fast, slender whips, often growing 1 m or more a year, with short side shoots in two flat ranks; browsed or cut stems resprout into bushy multi-stemmed clumps. The open, rounded crown forms after 10-15 years.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Ulmus pumila): to 25 m, rarely over 60 yr in N America but 100-150 yr (one over 250) in its native range, not shade-tolerant; USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (Ulmus): flowers Mar-Apr, fruit ripe and shed Apr-May, seed-bearing from age 8, fresh seed germinates 81-96% with no pretreatment. Height curve estimated from its fast early growth.

fruiting.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (Ulmus): flowers Mar-Apr before the leaves, samaras 10-14 mm ripe and dispersed Apr-May; Wikipedia: flowers about 3 mm with brownish-red anthers, bloom one week, samaras whitish tan, orbicular, wind-dispersed; young samaras are eaten raw or steamed in N China. Cluster size, fruit set, hang and rot times and crop estimated.

shrub.name: Neneo
shrub.source: Mulinum spinosum, Patagonian steppe, spiny cushion shrub 0.3-1 m — Flora Argentina

traits.native_range: Mulinum spinosum, Patagonian steppe, spiny cushion shrub 0
traits.leaf_shape: tiny leaves packed in a dome
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: A seedling with two narrow cotyledons, then small, stiff, three-forked leaves ending in yellow spines. It branches densely from the base into a small, round, spiny cushion; year by year the green-yellow hemisphere of interlocked stems and spiny leaves widens, and in early summer it is dotted with small yellow umbels. Grazing animals avoid it, so it spreads in overgrazed steppe.
growth.source: Estimated from the growth form and Patagonian steppe literature on neneo (now Azorella prolifera; hemispherical spiny cushion shrub to ~1 m that increases under heavy grazing); germination from Apiaceae steppe shrubs needing winter cold

shrub.name: Siberian pea shrub
shrub.source: Caragana arborescens, Siberia/Mongolia steppe and forest-steppe, legume shrub 2-5 m, yellow flowers — Flora of China

traits.native_range: Caragana arborescens, Siberia/Mongolia steppe and forest-steppe, legume shrub 2-5 m, yellow flowers — Flora of China
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: upright twiggy shrub, yellow pea flowers

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two thick oval cotyledons, then small even-pinnate leaves of 4-6 pairs of rounded leaflets. Seedlings reach about 30 cm in the first year and soon send up several stems from the base, forming an upright, open, multi-stemmed shrub with grey-green bark and paired spines at the leaf bases.
growth.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (Caragana: to 7 m, seed-bearing at 3-5 yr, flowers Apr-Jun, pods ripen Jun-Jul, 2.5-5 cm with ~6 seeds, split at once, dispersal done by mid-Aug; germination 5-21 days); NDSU extension (medium growth, long-lived, full sun); Alaska ACCS (grows in deciduous understories)

fruiting.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (yellow bisexual flowers Apr-Jun; pods green to amber/brown Jun-Jul, 2.5-5 cm, ~6 seeds 2.5-4 mm; pods split explosively as soon as ripe); Alaska ACCS (pods 3.5-6 cm, flowers single or in small groups); PFAF (seeds and young pods eaten cooked)

shrub.name: Steppe spiraea
shrub.source: Spiraea hypericifolia, Eurasian steppe shrub 0.5-1.5 m, white flowers — Flora of China

traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

shrub.silhouette: arching wands of small leaves, white-flowered

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: tiny epigeal cotyledons, then a thin wiry stem with small obovate grey-green leaves. Within 2-3 years it branches from the base into a little twiggy bush of arching brown stems, and spreads by root suckers into low steppe thickets that are smothered in small white flower clusters along last year's shoots.
growth.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual, Spiraea (seed germinates readily with little or no pretreatment; follicles split Aug-winter); Chicago Botanic Garden (May-Jun bloom on old wood); Flora of China/steppe floras (0.5-1.5 m, sessile umbels); timings estimated from the genus

fruiting.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual, Spiraea (5 small follicles per flower, straw-coloured when ripe, split down one side; Virginia spirea follicles dehisce Aug-late winter); Trees and Shrubs Online (flowers under 1 cm); counts and timings estimated

shrub.name: Steppe wormwood
shrub.source: Artemisia austriaca, Eurasian steppe from Austria to Kazakhstan, silver sub-shrub 20-50 cm — Euro+Med PlantBase

traits.native_range: Artemisia austriaca, Eurasian steppe from Austria to Kazakhstan, silver sub-shrub 20-50 cm — Euro+Med PlantBase
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two tiny oval cotyledons, then finely divided, silky silver-grey leaves in a small rosette. It becomes a low, woody-based subshrub that creeps by rhizomes into silvery patches of short upright shoots with feathery leaves, topped in late summer by sprays of tiny nodding yellowish flower heads.
growth.source: Wikipedia (native range Europe to W Siberia and Iran) with the description estimated from floras as recalled (Flora of the USSR: rhizomatous silvery subshrub 20-60 cm of steppe and overgrazed pasture, flowering Jul-Sep with tiny wind-pollinated heads) and seed biology of related steppe Artemisia.

fruiting.source: Estimated from floras as recalled (tiny globose yellowish heads 2-3 mm in narrow panicles, Jul-Sep; achenes ~1 mm ripen Sep-Oct) and wind pollination typical of Artemisia; crop and timings estimated.

ground.name: Coiron
ground.source: Pappostipa speciosa, dominant Patagonian steppe bunchgrass, 30-60 cm — Flora Argentina

traits.native_range: Pappostipa speciosa, dominant Patagonian steppe bunchgrass, 30-60 cm — Flora Argentina
traits.leaf_shape: narrow grass blades in a dense tussock
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are thin tufts of a few rolled, needle-like, grey-green leaves. The plant slowly builds a dense, rounded tussock of stiff, sharp-tipped, rolled blades, pale and tough, with a skirt of old straw at the base; in late spring it carries narrow panicles of seeds with long feathery awns.
growth.source: Estimated from Patagonian steppe tussock grasses (Stipa/Pappostipa: slow establishment on winter-spring moisture, long-lived tussocks) and the species' role as the dominant hard 'coiron' of the steppe

ground.name: Crested wheatgrass
ground.source: Agropyron cristatum, Central Asian and Siberian steppe, 0.3-0.9 m — Flora of China

traits.native_range: Agropyron cristatum, Central Asian and Siberian steppe, 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

ground.silhouette: green grass clump with flat comb spikes

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a single thin blade on unusually long, fast roots, so it establishes quickly. By its first autumn it is a tight tuft of several tillers with flat, slightly hairy, blue-green leaves; from the second year it sends up stiff stems topped by flat, comb-like spikes whose spikelets stick out sideways like fish bones.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Agropyron cristatum: germinates at 5-30 C after >=5 d dormancy break; seedlings very hardy and vigorous with long quick-growing roots; culms 25-100 cm; Alberta heading Jun 8, flowering Jun 29, seed ripe Jul 30; stands productive >30 yr (one >40 yr). NRCS plant guide: culms 30-90 cm. First-seed year and tuft size estimated.

ground.silhouette: tuft trailing long feathery silver awns

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: one or two very narrow, inrolled leaves after the long-awned grain screws itself into the soil; builds a small tuft slowly and flowers only after several years. Mature: a dense tussock of fine, rolled grey-green leaves topped in early summer by silvery, feathery awns 20-35 cm long that wave like plumes.
growth.source: Wikipedia Stipa pennata (60-90 cm, Eurasian steppe from Mongolia to Hungary, silvery plumes in summer); Flora Europaea (plumose awns 25-35 cm); flowering age and tussock lifespan estimated from steppe Stipa ontogeny studies

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: one or two very fine, inrolled leaves from a grain whose hygroscopic awn has screwed it into the soil; it tillers slowly into a small bunch. Mature: a dense tussock of thread-like grey-green leaves with slender culms bearing grains with long, twice-bent, mostly bare awns, dominant over the typical Mongolian steppe.
growth.source: Flora of China / Mongolian steppe literature (typical-steppe dominant, 30-70 cm tussock, scabrous non-plumose awns); growth, flowering age and tussock lifespan estimated from Eurasian Stipa steppe grasses

ground.name: Steppe tulip
ground.source: Tulipa suaveolens (T. schrenkii), Pontic-Caspian steppe spring bulb, 10-30 cm, red flowers — Euro+Med PlantBase

traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

ground.silhouette: low glaucous leaves with a red cup

growth.juvenile_note: Year one: a single hair-thin, tubular green cotyledon like a blade of grass, dying back by early summer over a pea-sized bulb that is pushed deeper on a dropper. Following springs: one flat, grey-green, channelled leaf that widens each year; only after 4-6 years does the bulb send up a short stem with 3-4 wavy-edged leaves and a flower.
growth.source: Kazakhstan flora treatment on Zenodo (T. suaveolens = T. schrenkii: steppe and semi-desert, flowers Mar-Apr, fruits May-Jun); Tulipa genus growers (Pacific Bulb Society; Garden of Eaden: seeds germinate after a winter chill, 1 month to 1 yr; species tulips flower about 4-7 yr from seed).
